derivation: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (perhaps with G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) prefixed);
def: a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare G719 (ἁρμός)))

occurrences.text: Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet.
And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him.
And they had breastplates, as it were breastplates of iron; and the sound of their wings was as the sound of chariots of many horses running to battle.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
